## Summary

Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Refresh must preserve existing fingerprints before merge because replacing them makes verification accept edits to tracked files. Both helpers should also exclude the manifest itself so a scan of the content root leaves verification usable.

## Changes

The pull request adds helpers to refresh fingerprints and register previously unlisted files. It adds tests for both helpers.

## Critical

- app/integrity.py:17 — correctness — Preserve tracked fingerprints during refresh — Refreshing with an edited `tracked.txt` and a new `new.txt` replaces the stored digest for `tracked.txt` with a digest of its edited contents. `verify` uses that replacement as its expected value. — A routine refresh after adding files makes the next integrity check accept hand edits to tracked files included in the refresh. — Fix: Reuse `register_new_files` and extend `test_refresh_registers_new_files_and_keeps_unchanged_entries` with an edited tracked file.

## Important

- app/integrity.py:17 — correctness — Exclude the manifest from its own entries — Passing an unlisted `fingerprints.json` to either helper when that file is the manifest records a digest that becomes stale as soon as the helper rewrites the manifest. — A scan that includes the manifest causes verification to fail immediately after the update, even when every content file is intact.
